questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country and because I have already lived in the U.S I wanted to try and experience Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, I got an e-mail with all the information and I was able to sign up for orientation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation week where we got information and mingled with other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Me and 2 other students from my class rented an Airbnb together off campus which was really expensive but around the same price as what we would have been offered at campus. It is really hard to find anything else than Airbnb as most apartments and rentals have a minimum of 1 year lease. 
Due to Covid we were not promised housing on campus before July, which was way too late as we arrived in August.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think there are pros and cons about living off campus. If you pick a nice Airbnb you will get a much better place for the same price as on campus, as the on campus facilities looked horrible. However, by living on campus it is easier to get friends and you are closer to everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was way too late to offer housing in July, as we already had a place by that time. The other exchange students we talked to who had on campus housing, paid around 1000$ per room which was split with 4-5 other people and it was a really old and outdated accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was okay. The university emailed us a month before with the information, however, the classes you could take was extremely limited as an exchange student which made it really hard. I had to register for classes around 4 times because there were something wrong each time even though I had elective courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to email the administration but it was a little frustrating as they had a few days of response time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get any of the classes I wanted and therefore had to pick what was available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can only take classes at Main Campus and classes with no prerequisites and you can only do essay courses and half year courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was okay but there is so much more work than on KU. You have to take around 4-5 classes for a semester and each class requires you to do work every week besides reading like a weekly quiz, essay, discussion posts and tests.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different, you are less independent in your studies as there is always something you have to do, like a quiz in one course every sunday evening which makes it hard to plan your own time as it has been planned for you already. You kinda just have to do everything when the professors want you to whereas at KU you can kinda plan your own time as long as you get it done.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and Fashion 
American Nightmare/Politics
Power, Oppression and Privilege/Philosophy
Mystery and Detective Fiction/English

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend American Nightmare, we had a really nice professor and it was an interesting course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Phone plans are very expensive in Canada as well as groceries. You also have to tip, so that is an extra cost always when eating out, going to the hair dresser and stuff like that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Phone plans
Groceries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs you could sign up for. I signed up for the outdoors club but they release their trips on random times so if you don't notice within an hour it will be filled up. I missed out on a trip because I was taking a nap.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I've heard really good things about the Outdoors club. They usually have a lot more to offer than when I was there, but unfortunately they have been suffering under the pandemic too. They have some cool trips so make sure to keep an eye out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Toronto or Niagara Falls

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: If you are used to Canada or the United States you will already know the differences and then it is pretty easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure to go to the orientation and participate in the events they offer, it'll make it easier to make friends as everyone is kinda in the same situation looking for friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't really find it challenging but people are a lot more offended by things here than in Denmark, so try and be respectful of that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open and friendly and you can always find a friendly stranger.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't think too much about school, you will learn just as much by exploring a new culture and being on your own, so as long as you do what is required you need to try and experience the rest after. 
2. Go travel as much as you can.
3. Make a lot of friends from different places.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think being on your own in a foreign country is a good challenge for yourself and you get to learn a lot about yourself and grow from it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge is being away from everyone you know on big days, but try and distract yourself by going out with your friends or traveling, because then you won't really notice.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
